messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: eng-oncall paged for SEV2 - GPU OOMs during prefill in us-west-2 cluster (model: gpt-redwood-32k). Several containers restarted in the last 8m. Error: "CUDA runtime error (2): out of memory" reported by runtime. Logs attached below.

Mike (oncall): saw the alert, jumping in. Is this spiking or steady?

Alex P: We're seeing a surge of long-context requests (users hitting ~28k tokens). Prefill step allocates KV cache and often spikes memory before generation. Multiple pods hit OOM and k8s restarted containers.

Sana R: Confirmed in logs:
```
E tensorflow: /workspace/runtime/ops/allocator.cc: failed to allocate 12GB
runtime_error: CUDA out of memory. Allocated 20GB, tried to allocate 12GB
Container restart reason: OOMKilled
```

Mike (oncall): OK. Initial mitigation suggestions?

Alex P: Short-term: 1) divert traffic to smaller-context variant (gpt-redwood-8k) via routing policy 2) scale up node pool with larger GPUs to absorb in-flight requests 3) apply prefill token cap at runtime to reject >16k prefill requests.

Taylor (eng-sre): I'm launching a policy change to route new requests to 8k variant for customers without strict context needs. Patching routing now.

Priya M: Doing canary first. Will update the service discovery to prefer 8k for non-enterprise tenants.

deploy-bot: Routing change submitted: service/routing-config#487 applied to canary (10% traffic). Status: SUCCESS. :rocket:

Mike (oncall): Can we also reduce batch size on the prefill path? That lowers peak memory.

Alex P: Yes, reducing prefill batch_size from 16 -> 4 reduces KV allocation concurrency. I'll push a runtime flag. Patch ready:
```
PATCH /runtime/config
- prefill_batch_size: 16
+ prefill_batch_size: 4
+ prefill_token_limit: 16000
```

Sana R: Applying patch to canary pods now.

Jen (support): Heads up: Customers A and B reported increased error rates. I'm drafting a customer-facing note. Is the routing change expected to affect latency?

Alex P: Small impact on latency (~+30ms) for affected requests but prevents restarts. Worth it.

Taylor (eng-sre): Canary patch applied. Monitoring memory graphs. Early signs: drop in OOM events for canary nodes.

incident-bot: New alert suppressed for canary nodes.

Mike (oncall): How about in-flight requests that already started prefill >16k? Some pods may still die. Any plan for draining?

Alex P: We'll gracefully reject new prefill requests beyond 16k at the load balancer layer. For current in-flight long-prefill requests, SRE will cordon and drain affected pods and let requests finish where possible. If pod is unhealthy/blocked, we will terminate to avoid domino restarts.

Taylor (eng-sre): Executing cordon/drain on 3 nodes with repeated restarts. Commands run:
```
kubectl cordon n1-usw2-03 && kubectl drain n1-usw2-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl delete pod runtime-gpt-32k-7f9d --grace-period=60
```

Sana R: Patch to runtime compiled and uploaded. Deploying to remaining pods after canary ok.

deploy-bot: Runtime config rollout: 20% -> 50% -> 100%. Step 1: SUCCESS. Step 2: SUCCESS. Step 3: IN PROGRESS.

Mike (oncall): Support reply ready? Jen, paste your message here and we'll signoff.

Jen (support): Draft to customers: "We experienced GPU memory errors causing some requests with very large context windows to fail. We've routed traffic to a smaller-context model and applied protections that will reject extremely large prefill requests while we stabilize. You may see slightly higher latencies for some requests; no customer data was affected. We're monitoring and will follow up with a root cause analysis." Thoughts?

Alex P: Fine to send. Add ETA for RCA: 48h.

Jen (support): Sent to affected customers.

Taylor (eng-sre): Post-deploy: OOMs dropped to baseline. We still saw two pod restarts tied to older in-flight long-prefill sessions but no customer-visible degraded throughput.

Mike (oncall): Closing loop: Severity downgraded to SEV3 at 17m after initial page. Confirm there were restarts but no lasting outage.

Priya M: Adding follow-ups: 1) enforce per-tenant prefill hard limit in load balancer 2) add telemetry to count prefill token distribution spikes 3) revisit model variant defaults in routing to prefer 8k for unknown clients.

Alex P: Also propose a longer-term fix: implement streaming prefill that does incremental KV persistence to avoid large transient allocations, and enable quantized KV cache for 32k model. I'll add to backlog.

Taylor (eng-sre): Creating incident ticket and postmortem skeleton. assigned: Taylor, Alex, Priya, Jen.

Mike (oncall): Handing off to Alex for postmortem writeup. Next oncall: Priya M (starts in 50m).

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager closed by Mike (oncall). Summary: GPU OOMs during prefill due to spike of long-context requests; mitigations: routing to 8k variant, prefill caps, reduce batch_size; severity downgraded.

Jen (support): Closing customer loop: sent update and ETA for RCA.

Alex P: I'll draft the RCA and link here when ready. Action items logged in incidents/2261001234.

Taylor (eng-sre): Postmortem link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2261001234/postmortem (draft)

Priya M: Adding monitoring alert to catch >5% of requests with prefill length >16k per minute.

Mike (oncall): Thanks all. Leaving notes in the oncall log. :white_check_mark:
